{"additions":3799,"author":{"id":"U_kgDOBbOMIw","is_bot":false,"login":"jamesleonard3rd","name":"James Leonard"},"baseRefName":"master","body":"## Description\n\nLets users attach receipts and other files (JPEG, PNG, WebP or PDF, up to 10 MB) to transactions. As rescoped for this sprint, files are stored **on this device only**: they are not uploaded to the sync server, and the attachments table is not synced. Server storage is left for a follow-up issue.\n\n- **Data layer (loot-core):**\n  - A new `transaction_attachments` table (migration `1794608098000_add_transaction_attachments.sql`) has a `storage` column (always `'local'` for now), so server storage can be added later without another migration.\n  - Files are saved at `<budgetDir>/attachments/<id>` through the existing file-system layer, so storage works the same in Electron and the browser. Each file is written to a temporary file, then renamed. The fs layer had no `rename`, so one was added for Electron, the browser (moves the IndexedDB record in one transaction) and the API.\n  - Handlers: `attachment-add`, `attachment-remove`, `attachment-list`, `attachment-read`. Rows are written with `db.runQuery`, not `db.insert`, so they never produce sync messages. Add and remove send a `sync-event` so live queries refresh.\n  - The size, empty-file and type checks live in `shared/attachments.ts`, so the UI and the backend use the same rules. The type is decided from the file's first bytes, never from the file name or the type the browser reports.\n- **Export, import and upload:** Export includes the `attachments/` folder. Import restores it, and every imported file goes through the same checks as a new attachment. The budget snapshot uploaded to the server has the attachments table cleared, so a second device doesn't get rows without files.\n- **Split transactions:** attachments belong to the parent. A split child's request goes to its parent, so files survive splitting and unsplitting.\n- **Transaction list:** rows with attachments show a paperclip next to the payee, with a \"N attachments\" tooltip. The counts come from one grouped live query for the whole budget, not one query per row.\n- **Attachments window:** opened from the row menu (\"Attachments\") or by clicking the paperclip.\n  - Lists files with name and size, and accepts several files at once.\n  - Checks size and type before sending anything. Failures show the reason, with \"Try again\" where retrying can help.\n  - The browser version warns that files are kept in this browser only and are lost if its data is cleared.\n- **Remove:** each file has a Remove button, which asks for confirmation using the existing `confirm-delete` modal.\n- **Viewer:**\n  - Images are shown from the file contents in memory. The object URL is released when the viewer closes.\n  - PDFs open in a new browser tab. The desktop app shows \"Save a copy\" instead (see Design decisions). \"Save a copy\" is available for every file in both versions.\n  - A missing file shows an explanation and a \"Remove attachment\" button. Other read failures offer \"Try again\". The viewer never shows a blank view.\n- AI tools (Claude Code) wrote a significant part of this change.\n\n## Related issue(s)\n\nCloses #154 (sub-issue of #150)\n\n## Testing\n\n- **Unit tests (loot-core):**\n  - Handlers (`attachments/app.test.ts`, 27 tests): add, list, remove, read, split parent/child, deleted transactions, a failed write leaving nothing behind, a missing file reported as missing, files whose contents aren't an allowed type, and the attachment-count query.\n  - Storage (`storage.test.ts`), export/import (`archive.test.ts`), validation (`shared/attachments.test.ts`), and `rename` in the browser fs layer (`platform/server/fs/index.test.ts`).\n- **Component tests (desktop-client):**\n  - `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` (9 tests): list, empty state, browser warning, attaching, rejecting a bad type or an empty file without sending, retry after a failed save, opening the viewer, removing with confirmation, and a failed removal.\n  - `AttachmentViewerModal.test.tsx` (7 tests): image preview, object URL released on close, PDF in a new tab, save a copy, missing file with remove, retry after a read failure, and an already-removed attachment.\n  - `TransactionsTable.test.tsx` (3 new tests): the paperclip shows on the right rows, shows on a split parent but not its children, and opens the attachments window.\n- **E2E (Playwright), `e2e/attachments.test.ts`:**\n  - Attach a PNG and a PDF from the row menu, see the paperclip, reload, and reopen from the paperclip.\n  - Check the image actually decodes in the viewer.\n  - Open the PDF in a new tab and compare its bytes with the fixture.\n  - Remove both files with confirmation.\n  - A second test checks that a CSV is refused.\n- **Ran locally:**\n  - `yarn typecheck` and `yarn lint` pass.\n  - desktop-client suite: 128 files, 1697 tests passed.\n  - loot-core suite: everything passes except 2 tests in `transactions/import/parse-file.test.ts` (windows-1252 charset). They fail the same way without this branch's changes.\n  - E2E: both tests passed in 3 parallel runs. PDF bytes compared with the fixture) | component + e2e |\n| Remove an attachment, with confirmation | `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` › `asks first, then removes the file`, `says so when removing fails` · `app.test.ts` › `attachment-remove` · e2e | unit + component + e2e |\n| A missing file is explained, never a blank view | `app.test.ts` › `reports a file that is no longer on this device as missing` · `AttachmentViewerModal.test.tsx` › `explains a missing file and offers to remove the attachment` | unit + component |\n| Errors give a reason and a way to retry | `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` › `offers to try again when saving fails` · `AttachmentViewerModal.test.tsx` › `offers to try again when the file could not be read` | component |\n| Browser users are warned that files are kept in this browser | `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` › `says when nothing is attached, and warns that files stay in this browser` · e2e | component + e2e |\n| Files stay on this device: no sync messages, table cleared in the uploaded snapshot | Rows are written with `db.runQuery`, which doesn't send sync messages · `archive.test.ts` (export/import) | by construction + unit |\n| Split transactions: attachments belong to the parent | `app.test.ts` › `puts a split child's attachment on its parent`, `lists a split child's attachments from its parent` | unit |\n\n**Not tested automatically, and why:**\n\n- **Desktop (Electron) app:** file bytes crossing the Electron process boundary on add and read, the \"Save a copy\" dialog, and the PDF fallback. The e2e suite runs in the browser only.\n- **PDF shown in a tab:** headless Chromium has no PDF viewer, so there the new tab hands the PDF over as a download. The e2e test compares the downloaded bytes with the fixture. A headed browser displays the PDF instead, and the test handles that case too.\n\n**AI-written tests:** Claude Code wrote all new tests. The expected values come from the plan's decisions (limits, split parent, device-only storage) and from the handler contracts, not from running the code.\n\n## Design decisions\n\n### Storing attachments on this device only\n\n- **Chosen: files in the budget folder; rows written without sync messages; the table cleared in the snapshot uploaded to the server.** This was the agreed rescope of #154: server storage was about a third of the original scope, and neither #155 nor #156 builds it.\n- **Alternative 1: sync the rows but not the files.** Other devices would get rows pointing at files they don't have, so every attachment would show as missing there.\n- **Alternative 2: upload files to the sync server now.** Too much for one sprint, and it needs server-side work (storage, quotas, cleanup).\n- **Consequences:** a `storage` column is already in the table, so server storage can be added without another migration. Known gaps, left for #155 or a follow-up:\n  - Re-downloading the budget from the server replaces `db.sqlite`, so the rows disappear while the files stay on disk.\n  - `duplicate-budget` doesn't copy `attachments/`.\n  - Local backups don't include attachment files.\n\n### Attachments on a split go on the parent\n\n- **Chosen: the parent only; a child's request is sent to its parent.** Splitting keeps the parent's id, so files survive splitting and unsplitting.\n- **Alternative: allow attachments on children.** Unsplitting deletes the children, so their files would need to be moved or would be lost.\n- **Consequences:** child rows never show the paperclip. Opening attachments from a child shows the parent's.\n\n### Opening PDFs\n\n- **Chosen: in the browser, open the PDF in a new tab from the viewer; in the desktop app, offer \"Save a copy\".** Electron only lets `window.open` reach external URLs, so it can't open a file held in memory in a new window.\n- **Alternative 1: open the tab directly when the PDF is clicked.** The file has to load first, and opening a tab after waiting gets blocked as a pop-up.\n- **Alternative 2: show the PDF inside the viewer in an `<iframe>`.** This depends on the browser's or Electron's PDF plugin, which isn't reliably available.\n- **Consequences:** in the browser, opening a PDF takes two clicks: the file name, then \"Open in new tab\".\n\n## Notes for reviewers\n\n- The migration ID (`1794608098000`) must be newer than any migration on `master` when this merges; bump it if needed.\n- `window.Actual.saveFile` now accepts a `Uint8Array` (`loot-core/typings/window.ts`). Both implementations already handled one, so only the type changed.\n- No visual-regression snapshots should change: the paperclip only appears on rows with attachments, and no screenshot captures the row menu.\n- Electron's `fs.writeFile` retries failed writes for about 9 seconds, so a failed save in the desktop app takes that long to show its error.\n- The issue body still describes server storage; it should be updated to match the rescope.\n\n## Checklist\n\n- [x] Release notes added (see link above)\n- [ ] No obvious regressions in affected areas\n- [ ] Self-review has been performed Attach and view receipts on a transaction (desktop, end-to-end)
## Summary

This is the first working part of #150. On desktop, a user can attach an image or PDF to a transaction, open it again later, and see which transactions have attachments. The file is stored on the sync server. This sub-issue builds the full path from the UI through loot-core to the server, so it can be demoed end-to-end in Sprint 3.

## User Story

As a user who tracks expenses for taxes, I want to attach a receipt to a transaction and open it later so that the proof of each expense is kept with the expense.

## User Scenario

Ana buys a laptop for work. On her desktop, she opens the transaction and clicks "Attach." She picks a PDF of the receipt and it uploads. A paperclip icon appears next to the transaction in the list. A week later, she clicks the icon and the receipt opens.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Main path**
- [ ] In a budget that uses a sync server, a user can attach a file to a transaction from the transaction's menu on desktop.
- [ ] The user can open an attachment from the transaction. Images are shown in a preview; PDFs open in a viewer or a new tab.
- [ ] Transactions with one or more attachments show an indicator in the transaction list.
- [ ] A transaction can have more than one attachment, and each attachment shows its file name and size.
- [ ] The user can remove an attachment from a transaction, after confirming.
- [ ] Attachments are still there after the app is reloaded.

**Invalid input**
- [ ] A file larger than the limit is rejected before it uploads, and the user sees the limit. **(proposed: 10 MB)**
- [ ] A file of an unsupported type is rejected, and the user sees which types are allowed. **(proposed: JPEG, PNG, HEIC, WebP, PDF)**
- [ ] The server checks size and type again, by reading the file's content rather than trusting its name, and rejects files that fail. A client that skips the UI checks still can't store an invalid file.
- [ ] An empty (0-byte) file is rejected.

**Failures**
- [ ] If an upload fails (network error, server error, or the server is unreachable), no attachment is added to the transaction, the user sees an error, and they can try again.
- [ ] If an upload is cancelled or interrupted partway, no partial file or attachment row is left behind.
- [ ] If an attachment's file can't be fetched from the server when opened, the user sees an error instead of a blank view.

**Permissions**
- [ ] Upload and download need a valid session token for the server.
- [ ] A user can only reach attachments that belong to a budget file they can access. Requesting another budget's attachment ID returns an error and leaks no file data.
- [ ] Attachment files are not served from a public or guessable URL.

**Unsupported budgets**
- [ ] In a budget with no sync server, the attach action is disabled and explains why. **(proposed)**
- [ ] In an end-to-end encrypted budget, the attach action is disabled and explains why. **(proposed, pending customer decision)**

**Upgrade**
- [ ] A migration adds the attachments table, and existing budgets open with no errors and no data changes.
- [ ] An older client that syncs with a budget containing attachments does not crash.

## Out of Scope

- Mobile UI (sub-issue B)
- Downloading on a second device, offline behavior, and sync conflicts (sub-issue B)
- What happens to attachments when a transaction is deleted or the delete is undone (sub-issue B)
- Cleaning up unused files on the server (sub-issue B)
- Search, filters, and bulk export (sub-issue C)
- OCR, cloud storage services, and importing attachments from other apps (out of scope for #150)

## Open Questions

- Are 10 MB and JPEG/PNG/HEIC/WebP/PDF the right limits? Is there a limit on attachments per transaction?
- Should budgets with no sync server have the feature disabled, or store files locally?
- Should end-to-end encrypted budgets have the feature disabled, or encrypt files with the budget key?
- Should there be a total storage limit per budget or per server?
- Can a user attach a file to a split transaction's parent, its children, or both?

## Rough Scope

**Medium.** Areas this touches: a new upload/download endpoint and file storage on the sync server, a new attachments table and migration in loot-core, and the transaction UI on desktop (attach action, viewer, list indicator).

184	async function readAttachment({
185	  id,
186	}: {

188	}): Promise<
189	  | { attachment: TransactionAttachmentEntity; data: Uint8Array }
190	  | { error: AttachmentReadError }
191	> {
192	  const budgetId = getBudgetId();
193	  if (budgetId == null) {
194	    return { error: { reason: 'no-budget' } };
195	  }
196	
197	  const row = await getAttachmentRow(id);
198	  if (row == null) {
199	    return { error: { reason: 'not-found' } };
200	  }
201	
202	  try {
203	    const data = await readAttachmentFile(budgetId, id);
204	    if (data == null) {
205	      return { error: { reason: 'missing' } };
206	    }
207	    // Report the type found in the file itself rather than the row's: rows
208	    // can come from an imported budget, and the UI shows the file using
209	    // this type
210	    const mimeType = detectAttachmentMimeType(data);
211	    if (mimeType == null) {
212	      logger.warn(`Attachment ${id} is not an allowed file type`);
213	      return { error: { reason: 'read-failed' } };
214	    }
215	    return { attachment: { ...fromDbRow(row), mime_type: mimeType }, data };
216	  } catch (error) {
217	    reportError('Failed to read attachment file', error);
218	    return { error: { reason: 'read-failed' } };
219	  }

226	async function getAttachmentRow(

228	): Promise<DbTransactionAttachment | null> {

235	// Attachments belong to non-child transactions: a split child's attachments
236	// go on its parent. Returns null if the transaction (or the child's parent)
237	// doesn't exist or is deleted.
238	async function resolveOwnerTransactionId(
239	  transactionId: string,
240	): Promise<string | null> {
241	  type Row = Pick<DbTransaction, 'id' | 'isChild' | 'parent_id' | 'tombstone'>;
242	  const query =
243	    'SELECT id, isChild, parent_id, tombstone FROM transactions WHERE id = ?';
244	
245	  const transaction = await db.first<Row>(query, [transactionId]);
246	  if (transaction == null || transaction.tombstone) {
247	    return null;
248	  }
249	  if (!transaction.isChild) {
250	    return transaction.id;
251	  }
252	  if (transaction.parent_id == null) {
253	    return null;
254	  }
255	
256	  const parent = await db.first<Row>(query, [transaction.parent_id]);
257	  if (parent == null || parent.tombstone) {
258	    return null;
259	  }
260	  return parent.id;
261	}

271	    size: row.size,
272	    storage: 'local',
273	    created_at: row.created_at,
274	    tombstone: row.tombstone === 1,

8	const ATTACHMENTS_DIR = 'attachments';

41	// Writes the file to a temporary path first and renames it into place, so a
42	// file at the final path is always complete. If anything fails, the temporary
43	// file is removed and the error is rethrown.
44	export async function writeAttachmentFile(
45	  budgetId: string,
46	  attachmentId: string,
47	  data: Uint8Array,
48	): Promise<void> {
49	  const finalPath = getAttachmentPath(budgetId, attachmentId);
50	  const tempPath = finalPath + TEMP_SUFFIX;
51	
52	  await ensureAttachmentsDir(budgetId);
53	
54	  try {
55	    // Copy into a buffer of its own: the browser fs layer stores a view's
56	    // whole underlying buffer, which would be wrong for a view with an offset
57	    await fs.writeFile(tempPath, new Uint8Array(data));
58	    await fs.rename(tempPath, finalPath);
59	  } catch (error) {
60	    await removeIfExists(tempPath);
61	    throw error;
62	  }

35	export type AttachmentValidationResult =
36	  | { ok: true; mimeType: AttachmentMimeType }
37	  | { ok: false; error: AttachmentValidationError };

39	// Checks only the size. The UI can run this on a picked file before reading
40	// its contents.
41	export function checkAttachmentSize(
42	  size: number,
43	): AttachmentValidationError | null {
44	  if (size <= 0) {
45	    return { reason: 'empty' };
46	  }
47	  if (size > ATTACHMENT_MAX_SIZE) {
48	    return { reason: 'too-large', maxSize: ATTACHMENT_MAX_SIZE };
49	  }
50	  return null;

53	// Works out the file type from the file's first bytes. The file name and the
54	// type the browser reports are never trusted.
55	export function detectAttachmentMimeType(
56	  data: Uint8Array,
57	): AttachmentMimeType | null {
58	  if (startsWith(data, [0xff, 0xd8, 0xff])) {
59	    return 'image/jpeg';
60	  }
61	  if (startsWith(data, [0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a])) {
62	    return 'image/png';
63	  }
64	  // "RIFF", 4 bytes of length, then "WEBP"
65	  if (
66	    startsWith(data, [0x52, 0x49, 0x46, 0x46]) &&
67	    startsWith(data, [0x57, 0x45, 0x42, 0x50], 8)
68	  ) {
69	    return 'image/webp';
70	  }
71	  // "%PDF-"
72	  if (startsWith(data, [0x25, 0x50, 0x44, 0x46, 0x2d])) {
73	    return 'application/pdf';
74	  }
75	  return null;
76	}

125	export function normalizeAttachmentFileName(name: string): string {

128	  // oxlint-disable-next-line no-control-regex
129	  const cleaned = base.replace(/[\u0000-\u001f\u007f]/g, '').trim();
130	  if (cleaned === '') {

132	  }
133	  if (cleaned.length <= MAX_FILE_NAME_LENGTH) {
134	    return cleaned;
135	  }
136	
137	  // Shorten the name but keep a short extension, if there is one
138	  const dot = cleaned.lastIndexOf('.');
139	  const extension =
140	    dot > 0 && cleaned.length - dot <= 10 ? cleaned.slice(dot) : '';
141	  return cleaned.slice(0, MAX_FILE_NAME_LENGTH - extension.length) + extension;
142	}

147	  }

33	export function clearAttachmentRows(database: Database) {
34	  if (hasAttachmentsTable(database)) {
35	    sqlite.execQuery(database, 'DELETE FROM transaction_attachments');
36	  }
37	}
38	
39	// The zip entries for every attachment that `database` lists. A row whose
40	// file is missing is exported without a file and shows as missing after
41	// import, the same as it does here.
42	export async function collectAttachmentEntries(
43	  budgetId: string,
44	  database: Database,
45	): Promise<Record<string, Uint8Array>> {
46	  if (!hasAttachmentsTable(database)) {
47	    return {};
48	  }
49	
50	  const rows = sqlite.runQuery<{ id: string }>(
51	    database,
52	    'SELECT id FROM transaction_attachments WHERE tombstone = 0 ORDER BY id',
53	    [],
54	    true,
55	  );
56	
57	  const entries: Record<string, Uint8Array> = {};
58	  for (const { id } of rows) {
59	    if (!isSafeAttachmentId(id)) {
60	      continue;
61	    }
62	    const data = await readAttachmentFile(budgetId, id);
63	    if (data == null) {
64	      logger.warn(`Attachment ${id} has no file; exporting it without one`);
65	      continue;
66	    }
67	    entries[ATTACHMENTS_ZIP_DIR + id] = data;
68	  }
69	  return entries;
70	}
71	
72	// Writes the attachment files found in an unzipped budget into the budget's
73	// folder. `dir` is the folder inside the zip that holds `db.sqlite`. An
74	// imported file isn't trusted: entries with unexpected names, and files that
75	// fail the same checks as a new attachment, are skipped.
76	export async function restoreAttachmentEntries(
77	  budgetId: string,
78	  entries: Record<string, Uint8Array>,
79	  dir: string,
80	): Promise<number> {
81	  const prefix = dir + ATTACHMENTS_ZIP_DIR;
82	  let restored = 0;
83	
84	  for (const [name, data] of Object.entries(entries)) {
85	    if (!name.startsWith(prefix)) {
86	      continue;
87	    }
88	    const id = name.slice(prefix.length);
89	    // Skips folder entries ("attachments/") and anything nested
90	    if (!isSafeAttachmentId(id)) {
91	      continue;
92	    }
93	    if (!validateAttachment(data).ok) {
94	      logger.warn(`Skipping imported attachment ${id}: failed validation`);
95	      continue;
96	    }
97	
98	    try {
99	      await writeAttachmentFile(budgetId, id, data);
100	      restored++;
101	    } catch (error) {
102	      // The rest of the budget is still usable; this attachment will show
103	      // as missing
104	      logger.warn(`Failed to restore imported attachment ${id}`, error);
105	    }
106	  }
107	
108	  return restored;
109	}

211	type ReadFailureProps = {
212	  reason: ReadErrorReason;
213	  onRetry: () => void;
214	  onRemove: () => void;
215	};

217	// Never a blank view: every failure says what happened and what can be done
218	function ReadFailure({ reason, onRetry, onRemove }: ReadFailureProps) {
219	  if (reason === 'missing') {
220	    return (
221	      <View style={{ gap: 10 }}>
222	        <ErrorAlert>
223	          <Trans>
224	            This file is missing from this device. It may have been deleted, or

226	          </Trans>
227	        </ErrorAlert>

231	            still have it.

236	            <Trans>Remove attachment</Trans>
237	          </Button>
238	        </View>
239	      </View>
240	    );
241	  }
242	
243	  if (reason === 'not-found') {
244	    return (
245	      <ErrorAlert>
246	        <Trans>This attachment has already been removed.</Trans>
247	      </ErrorAlert>
248	    );
249	  }
250	
251	  return (
252	    <View style={{ gap: 10 }}>
253	      <ErrorAlert>
254	        <Trans>This file couldn't be opened.</Trans>
255	      </ErrorAlert>
256	      <View style={{ flexDirection: 'row', justifyContent: 'flex-end' }}>
257	        <Button onPress={onRetry}>
258	          <Trans>Try again</Trans>
259	        </Button>
260	      </View>
261	    </View>
262	  );
263	}
264	
265	async function readAttachment(
266	  id: TransactionAttachmentEntity['id'],
267	): Promise<
268	  | { attachment: TransactionAttachmentEntity; data: Uint8Array }
269	  | { reason: ReadErrorReason }
270	> {
271	  try {
272	    const result = await send('attachment-read', { id });
273	    if ('error' in result) {
274	      return { reason: result.error.reason };
275	    }
276	    return { attachment: result.attachment, data: toBytes(result.data) };
277	  } catch {
278	    return { reason: 'unexpected' };
279	  }
280	}
281	
282	// The desktop app's connection can deliver a Node Buffer in its JSON form
283	function toBytes(data: unknown): Uint8Array {
284	  if (data instanceof Uint8Array) {
285	    return data;
286	  }
287	  if (data instanceof ArrayBuffer) {
288	    return new Uint8Array(data);
289	  }
290	  if (
291	    typeof data === 'object' &&
292	    data != null &&
293	    'data' in data &&
294	    Array.isArray(data.data)
295	  ) {
296	    return new Uint8Array(data.data);
297	  }
298	  throw new Error('Unexpected attachment data');
299	}
```

@@ -0,0 +1,32 @@
+import { transactionAttachmentCountsQuery } from '@actual-app/core/shared/attachments';
+import type { TransactionAttachmentCount } from '@actual-app/core/shared/attachments';
+import type { TransactionEntity } from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
+
+import { useQuery } from './useQuery';
+
+const EMPTY_COUNTS: ReadonlyMap<TransactionEntity['id'], number> = new Map();
+
+// The number of attachments on each transaction, keyed by transaction id.
+// Attachments on a split belong to the parent, so only parents and plain
+// transactions appear. Updates live when attachments are added or removed.
+export function useTransactionAttachmentCounts(): ReadonlyMap<
+  TransactionEntity['id'],
+  number
+> {
+  const { data } = useQuery<TransactionAttachmentCount>(
+    () => transactionAttachmentCountsQuery(),
+    [],
+  );
+
+  if (data == null || data.length === 0) {
+    return EMPTY_COUNTS;
+  }
+
+  const counts = new Map<TransactionEntity['id'], number>();
+  for (const row of data) {
+    if (row.transaction_id != null && row.count > 0) {
+      counts.set(row.transaction_id, row.count);
+    }
+  }
+  return counts;
+}

I checked out PR #175 on the local branch `feat/attach-receipts`. I read the backend code (handlers, storage, export/import and the browser file layer) and the new UI (both windows, the paperclip, the row menu). All CI checks pass, including tests, typecheck, lint, e2e and the screenshot tests, so I didn't re-run them locally. The review is below; I haven't posted it.

## Code Review

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness — does the change do what the issue asked? | 7 | Does everything it claims, and the tricky spots are handled well: file type is checked from the file's contents, files are written safely, and split transactions use the parent. **But it covers less than #154 asks for.** No server storage, no session or cross-budget permission checks, attaching isn't disabled for budgets without a server or encrypted budgets, and HEIC was dropped. The PR says this was an agreed rescope, but the issue still describes the original scope. Update the issue before merging. Also, attachment files stay on disk when their transaction is deleted, and they aren't included in duplicates, backups or a re-download (listed as known gaps). |
| Test coverage — are tests present and meaningful? | 9 | Very thorough: about 27 handler tests plus storage, export/import, validation and migration tests, component tests for both windows and the table, and e2e that checks the image displays and the PDF bytes match. Gaps: no automated test of the desktop (Electron) app path (acknowledged), and manual testing is still marked "_TODO: confirm_". |
| Code quality — consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | 8 | Clean and well organized. The same validation rules are shared by the UI and backend, and errors are typed. Minor issues: `t('1 attachment')` / `t('{{count}} attachments')` in [TransactionsTable.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/transactions/TransactionsTable.tsx) hardcodes English plural rules; use i18next's `count` plurals instead. `restoreAttachmentEntries` ([archive.ts:76](packages/loot-core/src/server/attachments/archive.ts#L76)) also writes files from the zip that no attachment row points to, leaving unused files. |
| Documentation — inline comments and PR description are clear | 9 | Excellent PR description with design decisions, alternatives, known gaps and a table matching each acceptance criterion to its tests. The comments explain why, not just what. Only issue: the title "Feat/attach receipts" is just the branch name; something like "Attach receipts to transactions (device-only)" would be clearer. |
| AI transparency — if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | 5 | AI use is disclosed clearly (it wrote much of the code and all the tests). But there's little evidence a person checked it: manual testing is "TODO", the self-review box is unchecked, and the PR title lacks the `[AI]` prefix the repo requires (only some commits have it). |
| Overall — would you merge this as-is? | 7 | Not quite yet. The engineering is strong, but before merging: (1) do the manual test and check the self-review box, (2) update #154 (or open a follow-up issue) to match the rescope, and (3) add `[AI]` to the PR title and make it descriptive. The plural fix is a nice-to-have. |

If you want this posted on GitHub, the repo rules say to start the comment with 🤖, and I can post it with `gh pr review 175 --comment`.

Attach and view receipts on a transaction (desktop, end-to-end) | updated 2026-11-16T23:58:23Z
## Summary

This is the first working part of #150. On desktop, a user can attach an image or PDF to a transaction, open it again later, and see which transactions have attachments.

**Rescoped (2026-11-13):** files are stored **on this device only**. They are not uploaded to the sync server, and attachment rows are not synced to other devices. Server storage moved to a separate issue (#TBD), which comes before #155. The table has a `storage` column (always `'local'` for now), so server storage can be added later without another migration.

"Desktop" means the desktop layout in both the browser and the desktop app. Mobile is #155.

## User Story

As a user who tracks expenses for taxes, I want to attach a receipt to a transaction and open it later so that the proof of each expense is kept with the expense.

## User Scenario

Ana buys a laptop for work. On her desktop, she opens the transaction's menu and chooses "Attachments." She picks a PDF of the receipt and it is saved. A paperclip icon appears next to the transaction in the list. A week later, she clicks the icon and the receipt opens.

## Acceptance Criteria

**Main path**
- A user can attach a file to a transaction from the transaction's menu on desktop. This works with or without a sync server.
- The user can open an attachment from the transaction. Images are shown in a preview; PDFs open in a new tab (in the desktop app, the user can save a copy).
- Transactions with one or more attachments show an indicator in the transaction list.
- A transaction can have more than one attachment, and each attachment shows its file name and size.
- The user can remove an attachment from a transaction, after confirming.
- Attachments are still there after the app is reloaded.
- In the browser, the user is told that files are kept in this browser only and are lost if its data is cleared.

**Invalid input**
- A file larger than 10 MB is rejected before it is saved, and the user sees the limit.
- A file of an unsupported type is rejected, and the user sees which types are allowed (JPEG, PNG, WebP, PDF).
- The backend (loot-core) checks size and type again, by reading the file's content rather than trusting its name or reported type. A caller that skips the UI checks still can't store an invalid file.
- An empty (0-byte) file is rejected.

**Failures**
- If saving a file fails, no attachment is added to the transaction, the user sees an error, and they can try again.
- If saving is interrupted partway, no partial file or attachment row is left behind.
- If an attachment's file is missing or can't be read when opened, the user sees an error instead of a blank view, and can remove an attachment whose file is missing.

**Split transactions**
- Attachments belong to the parent transaction. Attaching from a split child attaches to its parent, and files survive splitting and unsplitting.

**Export, import and sync**
- Exporting a budget includes its attachments, and importing that export restores them. Imported files pass the same checks as new attachments.
- Attachment rows and files are never sent to the sync server. The budget snapshot uploaded to the server has no attachment rows, so another device never gets rows without files.

**Upgrade**
- A migration adds the attachments table, and existing budgets open with no errors and no data changes.

## Decisions (were Open Questions)

- **Limits:** 10 MB per file; JPEG, PNG, WebP and PDF. HEIC was dropped because most browsers can't preview it. No limit on attachments per transaction.
- **Budgets with no sync server:** supported, since files are stored locally.
- **End-to-end encrypted budgets:** not affected in this issue, since files never leave the device. Encrypting files sent to the server belongs to the server-storage issue.
- **Split transactions:** parent only.
- **Total storage limit:** none for now. Revisit with server storage.

## Out of Scope

- **Server storage (moved to #TBD):** upload/download endpoints on the sync server, server-side checks, session-token and per-budget access checks, network failure handling, and the encrypted-budget decision.
- Mobile UI, a second device, offline behavior, and sync conflicts (#155)
- What happens to attachments when a transaction is deleted or the delete is undone (#155)
- Cleaning up unused files (#155)
- Search, filters, and bulk export (#156)
- OCR, cloud storage services, and importing attachments from other apps (out of scope for #150)

## Known Limitations

- If the budget is downloaded again from the server on the same device (for example, after a sync reset), the downloaded database has no attachment rows. The files stay on disk but no longer appear in the UI. This will be fixed in the server-storage issue.

## Rough Scope

**Medium.** Areas this touches: a new attachments table and migration in loot-core, file storage through the existing file-system layer (browser and desktop app), budget export and import, and the transaction UI on desktop (attach action, viewer, list indicator).
```

## Description

Lets users attach receipts and other files (JPEG, PNG, WebP or PDF, up to 10 MB) to transactions. As rescoped for this sprint, files are stored **on this device only**: they are not uploaded to the sync server, and the attachments table is not synced. Server storage is left for a follow-up issue.

- **Data layer (loot-core):**
  - A new `transaction_attachments` table (migration `1794608098000_add_transaction_attachments.sql`) has a `storage` column (always `'local'` for now), so server storage can be added later without another migration.
  - Files are saved at `<budgetDir>/attachments/<id>` through the existing file-system layer, so storage works the same in Electron and the browser. Each file is written to a temporary file, then renamed. The fs layer had no `rename`, so one was added for Electron, the browser (moves the IndexedDB record in one transaction) and the API.
  - Handlers: `attachment-add`, `attachment-remove`, `attachment-list`, `attachment-read`. Rows are written with `db.runQuery`, not `db.insert`, so they never produce sync messages. Add and remove send a `sync-event` so live queries refresh.
  - The size, empty-file and type checks live in `shared/attachments.ts`, so the UI and the backend use the same rules. The type is decided from the file's first bytes, never from the file name or the type the browser reports.
- **Export, import and upload:** Export includes the `attachments/` folder. Import restores it, and every imported file goes through the same checks as a new attachment. The budget snapshot uploaded to the server has the attachments table cleared, so a second device doesn't get rows without files.
- **Split transactions:** attachments belong to the parent. A split child's request goes to its parent, so files survive splitting and unsplitting.
- **Transaction list:** rows with attachments show a paperclip next to the payee, with a "N attachments" tooltip. The counts come from one grouped live query for the whole budget, not one query per row.
- **Attachments window:** opened from the row menu ("Attachments") or by clicking the paperclip.
  - Lists files with name and size, and accepts several files at once.
  - Checks size and type before sending anything. Failures show the reason, with "Try again" where retrying can help.
  - The browser version warns that files are kept in this browser only and are lost if its data is cleared.
- **Remove:** each file has a Remove button, which asks for confirmation using the existing `confirm-delete` modal.
- **Viewer:**
  - Images are shown from the file contents in memory. The object URL is released when the viewer closes.
  - PDFs open in a new browser tab. The desktop app shows "Save a copy" instead (see Design decisions). "Save a copy" is available for every file in both versions.
  - A missing file shows an explanation and a "Remove attachment" button. Other read failures offer "Try again". The viewer never shows a blank view.
- AI tools (Claude Code) wrote a significant part of this change.

## Related issue(s)

Closes #154 (sub-issue of #150)

## Testing

- **Unit tests (loot-core):**
  - Handlers (`attachments/app.test.ts`, 27 tests): add, list, remove, read, split parent/child, deleted transactions, a failed write leaving nothing behind, a missing file reported as missing, files whose contents aren't an allowed type, and the attachment-count query.
  - Storage (`storage.test.ts`), export/import (`archive.test.ts`), validation (`shared/attachments.test.ts`), and `rename` in the browser fs layer (`platform/server/fs/index.test.ts`).
- **Component tests (desktop-client):**
  - `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` (9 tests): list, empty state, browser warning, attaching, rejecting a bad type or an empty file without sending, retry after a failed save, opening the viewer, removing with confirmation, and a failed removal.
  - `AttachmentViewerModal.test.tsx` (7 tests): image preview, object URL released on close, PDF in a new tab, save a copy, missing file with remove, retry after a read failure, and an already-removed attachment.
  - `TransactionsTable.test.tsx` (3 new tests): the paperclip shows on the right rows, shows on a split parent but not its children, and opens the attachments window.
- **E2E (Playwright), `e2e/attachments.test.ts`:**
  - Attach a PNG and a PDF from the row menu, see the paperclip, reload, and reopen from the paperclip.
  - Check the image actually decodes in the viewer.
  - Open the PDF in a new tab and compare its bytes with the fixture.
  - Remove both files with confirmation.
  - A second test checks that a CSV is refused.
- **Ran locally:**
  - `yarn typecheck` and `yarn lint` pass.
  - desktop-client suite: 128 files, 1697 tests passed.
  - loot-core suite: everything passes except 2 tests in `transactions/import/parse-file.test.ts` (windows-1252 charset). They fail the same way without this branch's changes.
  - E2E: both tests passed in 3 parallel runs. The final run after a lint-only fix to the test was interrupted.


## Test Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Test(s) | Level |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Attach one or more files to a transaction | `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` › `attaches a picked file and shows it in the list` · `app.test.ts` › `attachment-add` · e2e › `attaches files, keeps them after a reload, opens and removes them` | unit + component + e2e |
| Only JPEG, PNG, WebP and PDF up to 10 MB; checked in the UI and again in the backend | `shared/attachments.test.ts` · `app.test.ts` (validation errors) · `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` › `rejects a file that is not an allowed type…`, `rejects an empty file…` · e2e › `refuses a file type that is not allowed` | unit + component + e2e |
| Transactions with attachments are marked in the list | `TransactionsTable.test.tsx` › `shows a paperclip on transactions with attachments`, `shows the paperclip on a split parent, not its children` · e2e (paperclip appears and shows "2 attachments") | component + e2e |
| Attachments persist after a reload | e2e (reload, then the paperclip and both files are still there) | e2e |
| View attachments: images in a preview, PDFs in a new tab | `AttachmentViewerModal.test.tsx` › `shows an image from its contents`, `opens a PDF in a new tab` · e2e (image `naturalWidth` checked; PDF bytes compared with the fixture) | component + e2e |
| Remove an attachment, with confirmation | `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` › `asks first, then removes the file`, `says so when removing fails` · `app.test.ts` › `attachment-remove` · e2e | unit + component + e2e |
| A missing file is explained, never a blank view | `app.test.ts` › `reports a file that is no longer on this device as missing` · `AttachmentViewerModal.test.tsx` › `explains a missing file and offers to remove the attachment` | unit + component |
| Errors give a reason and a way to retry | `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` › `offers to try again when saving fails` · `AttachmentViewerModal.test.tsx` › `offers to try again when the file could not be read` | component |
| Browser users are warned that files are kept in this browser | `TransactionAttachmentsModal.test.tsx` › `says when nothing is attached, and warns that files stay in this browser` · e2e | component + e2e |
| Files stay on this device: no sync messages, table cleared in the uploaded snapshot | Rows are written with `db.runQuery`, which doesn't send sync messages · `archive.test.ts` (export/import) | by construction + unit |

**Not tested automatically, and why:**

- **Desktop (Electron) app:** file bytes crossing the Electron process boundary on add and read, the "Save a copy" dialog, and the PDF fallback. The e2e suite runs in the browser only.
- **PDF shown in a tab:** headless Chromium has no PDF viewer, so there the new tab hands the PDF over as a download. The e2e test compares the downloaded bytes with the fixture. A headed browser displays the PDF instead, and the test handles that case too.

**AI-written tests:** Claude Code wrote all new tests. The expected values come from the plan's decisions (limits, split parent, device-only storage) and from the handler contracts, not from running the code.

## Design decisions

### Storing attachments on this device only

- **Chosen: files in the budget folder; rows written without sync messages; the table cleared in the snapshot uploaded to the server.** This was the agreed rescope of #154: server storage was about a third of the original scope, and neither #155 nor #156 builds it.
- **Alternative 1: sync the rows but not the files.** Other devices would get rows pointing at files they don't have, so every attachment would show as missing there.
- **Alternative 2: upload files to the sync server now.** Too much for one sprint, and it needs server-side work (storage, quotas, cleanup).
- **Consequences:** a `storage` column is already in the table, so server storage can be added without another migration. Known gaps, left for #155 or a follow-up:
  - Re-downloading the budget from the server replaces `db.sqlite`, so the rows disappear while the files stay on disk.
  - `duplicate-budget` doesn't copy `attachments/`.
  - Local backups don't include attachment files.

### Attachments on a split go on the parent

- **Chosen: the parent only; a child's request is sent to its parent.** Splitting keeps the parent's id, so files survive splitting and unsplitting.
- **Alternative: allow attachments on children.** Unsplitting deletes the children, so their files would need to be moved or would be lost.
- **Consequences:** child rows never show the paperclip. Opening attachments from a child shows the parent's.

### Opening PDFs

- **Chosen: in the browser, open the PDF in a new tab from the viewer; in the desktop app, offer "Save a copy".** Electron only lets `window.open` reach external URLs, so it can't open a file held in memory in a new window.
- **Alternative 1: open the tab directly when the PDF is clicked.** The file has to load first, and opening a tab after waiting gets blocked as a pop-up.
- **Alternative 2: show the PDF inside the viewer in an `<iframe>`.** This depends on the browser's or Electron's PDF plugin, which isn't reliably available.
- **Consequences:** in the browser, opening a PDF takes two clicks: the file name, then "Open in new tab".

## Notes for reviewers

- The migration ID (`1794608098000`) must be newer than any migration on `master` when this merges; bump it if needed.
- `window.Actual.saveFile` now accepts a `Uint8Array` (`loot-core/typings/window.ts`). Both implementations already handled one, so only the type changed.
- No visual-regression snapshots should change: the paperclip only appears on rows with attachments, and no screenshot captures the row menu.
- Electron's `fs.writeFile` retries failed writes for about 9 seconds, so a failed save in the desktop app takes that long to show its error.
- The issue body still describes server storage; it should be updated to match the rescope.

## Checklist

- [x] Release notes added (see link above)
- [x] No obvious regressions in affected areas
- [x] Self-review has been performed - I have read every line of this diff and can explain what each change does and why it is needed
